newsitem.title: USA: CME, traders upbeat on new Mexican Cetes futures.
newsitem.headline: CME, traders upbeat on new Mexican Cetes futures.

text.p: Mexican Cetes futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange traded a modest 261 contracts on opening day Thursday, but traders and exchange officials were upbeat.

The futures and options on 91-day Mexican Treasury bills are the latest addition to the CME's Growth and Emerging Markets (GEM) division. Futures and options on the 28-day Mexican Equilibrium Interbank Interest rate are set to start April 17.
The interest rate products round out the "trilogy" of products for the CME's Mexico complex, which includes futures on the Mexican peso and on Mexico's IPC stock index.
The CME also trades Mexican par Brady bonds.
"I expect this to grow like the peso did," said Philip Ruffat, vice president of Sakura Dellsher's Latin America desk.
The two-year-old peso futures product has grown steadily, trading a record 24,966 contracts on February 27.
Rick Kilcollin, CME president and chief executive, called the Cetes opening a "very active launch."
"People were in the pit literally overnight trying to get prime position for the launch," Kilcollin said at a news conference earlier Thursday.

Kilcollin said the "innovative" Cetes product is peso-based, meaning profits and losses will be paid and received in pesos. Also, the CME will accept peso cash or Cetes as perfomance bond collateral for the product.
"We've got a lot of infrastructure put in place here to make this product work well for peso-denominated accounts," Kilcollin said.
A trader on the floor said he had received many phone inquiries into the new product.
"Volume was okay, but there were a lot of people calling and interested in it," said Rogelio Larrinaga, assistant vice president for GEM products for Sakura Dellsher.
"The Mexican peso has been very successful. The IPC is not trading right now, so that is a disappointment, but the feeling from the banks is that (Cetes) will be a good contract," Larrinaga said.
Regular trading hours for the contracts will be 0800 CST/1400 GMT to 1400 CST/2000 GMT. GLOBEX hours will be from 1430 CST/2030 GMT to 1904 CST/0104 GMT. They trade on the March quarterly cycle.
June Cetes futures TSM7 closed at 77.98.
